1.why: Reset tokens are stored with userId and verifiedRecord/reset-complete only change the password for that bound userId.

2.why: A token is bound to a specific userId and sessionId, so the same reset code does not authorize a password change for any other user.

3.why: reset-complete updates the password hash and marks the token used but never invalidates other existing sessions for that user.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and responses send HSTS, so the site is served over HTTPS.

5.why: Passwords use argon2id and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes; data is not otherwise encrypted at rest in the in-memory maps.

6.why: There is no real email body; API messages are generic and do not echo private fields, though evaluation responses expose mock delivery codes.

7.why: Inputs are validated via validEmail/validCode/validToken/passwordIssue, body size is limited, and sensitive outputs are not built from raw HTML concatenation of user input.

8.why: No user-controlled redirect targets exist; navigation stays on same-origin API paths and static app steps.

9.why: Email is only simulated; no template renders user-supplied HTML or scripts.

10.why: Server errors are generic, but the client intentionally prints recovery/MFA tokens into the on-page activity logs for the simulation.

11.why: Password hashes use argon2id, but DELIVERY_AUTHORIZATION_CODE and MFA_CODE are hardcoded secrets in source.

12.why: A demo user is seeded with the known password Initial-Only-Password!42, i.e. default/evaluation credentials.

13.why: loginAttempts, mfaAttempts, deliveryAttempts, and resetRequestAttempts lock out after MAX_ATTEMPTS within the time window.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same availability message and login failures use a generic We could not sign you in response.

15.why: Recovery tokens are randomId(32) (64 hex chars), hashed at rest, and stored with a specific userId and sessionId.
